rationale: Fix a public Node admission obligation grounded in the explicit step-order permission and no-prior-unapplied-change promise, while preserving the narrower caller-duty interpretation for review. The formal endpoint is proposal encoding/admission, not general consensus safety.

question.question: When a synchronous Node caller has persisted a Ready and used the documented early Advance permission, must a new configuration proposal still be dropped while a prior committed configuration change has neither been activated nor rejected?
question.importance: The A1 configuration proposal guard consumes an application acknowledgment whose source meaning is weaker than completed configuration activation. Admitting another configuration can allow subsequent formation under the unchanged voter set. The selected requirement is the public proposal-admission contract; inconsistent committed decisions or broader consensus safety would require separate evidence.
contexts: Synchronous Node with configuration validation enabled and no joint configuration
Persistence completed before Advance; actual configuration applications remain in Ready order
Finite deferral of first configuration activation, without rejecting it; no crash or role change during proposal interval
event_paths: Actual Campaign and first ProposeConfChange -> committed Ready -> completed persistence -> Node.Advance -> queued MsgStorageApplyResp -> internal applied acknowledgment
Second Node.ProposeConfChange -> stepLeader pendingConfIndex guard -> emitted configuration entry or dropped/replaced proposal
Later ApplyConfChange first, then subsequent committed configuration entries in order

The numbered Node usage steps instead explicitly allow Advance any time after persistence, before the configuration application step, and preserve order rather than requiring completion before Advance.
RawNode.Advance describes applied-and-saved progress, but the selected entry is Node; importing the stricter lower-level wording would erase the explicit Node permission.

question.trigger_rationale: The explicit step-order permission provides a concrete applicability basis beyond the generic snapshot example. Fix the narrower proposal-admission requirement and test the actual Node path with an independent activation record, preserving the alternative immediate-duty interpretation for review.

obligation.description: With configuration validation enabled, a synchronous Node must not accept a subsequent configuration proposal as a configuration log entry while a prior committed configuration change has neither been applied through ApplyConfChange nor rejected by the caller, including when the caller has persisted the Ready and used the documented permission to Advance before finishing application.

scope.description: Public Node configuration proposal admission during finite ordered application deferral after completed Ready persistence.
assumptions: Serialized Node event loop and public API calls.
Ready entries, HardState and snapshots are saved before Advance; no early outbound response delivery.
Caller eventually activates the first configuration and preserves inter-Ready application order; the first configuration is not rejected.
Configuration validation enabled; simple configuration changes outside joint state; stable leader during the selected interval.
excluded: General election safety, divergent application results or quorum intersection proof
Eventual success of a permitted proposal

parameters.faults: No crash; newly added peers may be absent

grounding.derivation: Node.ProposeConfChange states that configuration changes are dropped unless the leader is certain there is no prior unapplied configuration change. Node usage step 3 includes ApplyConfChange; step 4 explicitly allows Advance any time after persistence step 1, while preserving application order. Accordingly the selected Node contract permits finite early acknowledgment without treating a not-yet-activated and not-rejected configuration as applied for admission. A new configuration must not be accepted during that interval. This is a one-way rejection requirement, not a requirement that later proposals must succeed.
grounding.applicability: Public synchronous Node; configuration validation enabled; caller fully persists each Ready before Advance, eventually invokes ApplyConfChange in order for each accepted committed configuration, and does not reject the pending configuration. No dependency on peer health determines rejection.
unresolved: The immediate-before-Advance reading of ApplyConfChange whenever observed would constrain the explicit numbered permission; correspondence must address this counterinterpretation.
alternatives: An implementation could retain separate pending configuration activation state, or use another reliable completion signal; the requirement does not prescribe an internal field.

A configuration-specific documented restriction on early Advance would exclude this policy. No such explicit restriction was found in the captured Node usage steps; tests using activation first do not establish it.
RawNode or asynchronous worker callers have different completion duties and are excluded.

bindings.description: Configuration proposal decoding, pending-index guard and empty normal-entry substitution in the actual serialized leader consumer.

associations.rationale: Binds the public Node rejection promise to the actual consumer of internal application acknowledgment; the guard itself does not establish the normative requirement.

feedback.answered: Selected the proposal-admission contract as the narrow responsibility supported by Node documentation. Early-Advance permission is explicit in the numbered usage instructions; the mandatory ApplyConfChange duty remains a contrary interpretation to assess, rather than silently importing RawNode completion duties. The accepted map distinguishes acknowledgment from activation, and exploration supplies an actual-producer construction only.
remaining: Fix and freshly execute a direct check that correlates each second proposal to its emitted entry or explicit drop while independently recording whether the first configuration was activated or rejected at processing time.
Review the selected Node caller policy, oracle and actual observations together; keep any unresolved applicability issue visible.
feedback.rationale: A local implementation-contract endpoint is obtainable without manufacturing a multi-leader safety consequence. The control policies explain protections but must not turn permission into an obligation to commit or succeed.
